segments: NixOS is a Linux distribution based on the Nix package manager, developed and maintained by the NixOS Foundation. Its distinctive declarative configuration approach lets you define and manage the entire system through configuration files.

Traditional Linux distributions usually require you to install packages, edit configuration files, and enable services manually. In NixOS, all these operations are defined in a single configuration.nix file:

Pinning the configuration, dependency revisions, and build inputs lets you repeatedly build the system environment described by the declaration. Writable data, hardware differences, and nondeterministic builds still need separate handling. This means:
You can deploy the same declarative environment on different machines
Team development environments can stay consistent
Production and development environments can share the same dependency and configuration definitions
New build outputs do not overwrite old ones, and switching the system profile supports atomic updates
Activation scripts, service restarts, bootloaders, and writable data can still encounter failures; rollback is no substitute for backups
You can roll back to a previous working version at any time

switch activates the configuration immediately and makes it the boot default; boot only builds it and makes it the boot default, leaving the running system unchanged; test activates it immediately without adding it to the boot menu. NixOS Manual
When replacing a login manager or critical service, both switch and test may interrupt the current session. If you want the new configuration to apply at the next boot, you can use boot first:
Features of the Nix package manager:
Isolated package paths: different packages and versions do not overwrite one another; activation and program execution can still have side effects
Coexisting versions: different versions of the same software can exist at the same time
Garbage collection: automatically removes packages no longer in use
Binary caches: prebuilt packages can be installed quickly
Declarative configuration makes management and rollback straightforward
Custom builds containing only the required components
Choose a stable branch or unstable while retaining generation-based rollback
Learning NixOS requires an understanding of the following:
Nix language basics - for writing configuration files
The NixOS module system - how configuration options work
nixpkgs - how to use the Nix package collection
